targets.title: Students' Conceptions About 'Radiation': Results from an Explorative Interview Study of 9th Grade Students
targets.evidence_quote: Our trend study had two major aims: First, it was self-evident that we wanted to test whether or not certain students' ideas about radiation, in general, remained the same and would also be shown in a replicative study two years after the original study.
targets.outcome_quote: For students' conceptions about radiation in general and types of radiation other than nuclear, we would like to refer the reader to the analysis of our first study (Neumann & Hopf, 2012). All students' ideas presented in the previously cited article, for instance, the idea that radiation is always something harmful and artificial or the idea that light is not a type of radiation, were discovered again in the 2012-interviews.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The explicit stability test rediscovers all previously reported conceptions. Changes in frequencies of spontaneous associations address the separate Fukushima trend question rather than overturning the replicated conceptions.
